title: Spec
description: Output of Phase 1 (BA). Defines what to build and why.

issue_number.description: Tracker issue number. Accepts a string for an experiment run (/pipeline --dry-run), which uses an exp-<slug> placeholder instead of opening a tracker issue, and null before an id exists.

root_cause.description: For bugs only. Null for features.

requirements.description: What must be true when done

acceptance_criteria.description: Testable criteria QA maps to tests

impacted_packages.description: Package or app paths the change touches

out_of_scope.description: Explicitly excluded items to prevent drift

sibling_causes_considered.description: Class-of-bug survey: when a fix targets one instance of a class-shaped bug (browser-bound state, retry idempotency, CSRF, timezone, access-control bypass, etc.), enumerate other instances in the same flow stage and record whether the same root cause applies. Optional but expected for spec quality on multi-instance bug classes. See the knowledge store's class-of-bug catalogs for a canonical example.

name.description: Concrete name of the sibling surface, key, file, or pattern

reason.description: One sentence on why same root cause does or does not apply, and what was done about it

trivial.description: Legacy boolean, kept for backward compatibility. trivial: true implies risk_tier trivial.

risk_tier.description: Sets the pipeline shape. architectural is MANDATORY for data/security/compliance domains, schema migrations, access-control policy changes, shared-contract shape changes, and new auth/crypto/webhook/data-intake surfaces; the orchestrator promotes an under-tiered spec. standard runs constraint injection plus a single Dev thread plus a trimmed panel; trivial skips constraint injection too.

ab_build.description: Tier-3 escalation. When true, Phase 3 runs as a dual-build A/B (two independent implementations of the same fixed surface, judged blind, winner materialized with best-of-both grafts) instead of the single Dev thread. BA sets this ONLY when risk_tier is architectural AND two or more materially different implementation approaches are genuinely viable AND a wrong approach is expensive (blast radius or a safety/compliance surface). Roughly an order of magnitude more spend than the default single-writer-plus-adversarial-panel path, so it is a rare, deliberate instrument. Default false.

ab_build_rationale.description: Required when ab_build is true: one or two sentences naming the materially-different approaches in contention and why the wrong one is expensive. Null otherwise.

knowledge_drift_claims.description: Optional staleness claims for the Librarian to resolve at Phase 5.

ba_notes.description: One or two sentences of context for downstream agents

scope_drift_log.description: Appended during Phase 3 if scope drift adjudicated

experiment_id.description: Present only on an experiment run: the exp-<slug> placeholder id used in place of a tracker issue.

measured_state.description: Every number this spec asserts about the live system, each with its GRAIN stated. A figure whose grain is unstated is the shape that ships a double count: 'terminix.com 27' was entries across rows, while the question it was quoted to answer needed 18 distinct searches. Required at the architectural tier, and it is the ONLY authoritative source for numbers in the spec. Implementers treat any figure arriving in a message rather than this block as unverified and re-derive it. See evidence.md rule 11.

grain.description: What it counts, in words: rows, entries, distinct terms, blocks, nested elements. Two figures at different grains are never subtracted; a remainder between them is the grain difference wearing the costume of a finding.

window.description: The time span and population it was measured over

source.description: How it was derived, precisely enough to re-run: query, endpoint, or script, plus when

falsifiability_pass.description: The can-this-redden audit over the acceptance criteria, run BEFORE implementation begins. Its first run on one issue found four criteria that could not fail, including two written specifically to prevent unfalsifiable tests; two more surfaced in later rounds. Required at the architectural tier. See evidence.md rules 3, 3b and 18.

one_mutation_per_criterion.description: One named mutation per criterion, machine-checked to match the criterion list exactly. The mutation names the PROPERTY that must break, not the fix: a control worded as 'delete the rule and confirm it reddens' passed while proving nothing, because deleting the rule produced a third distinct value rather than a collision.

mutation.description: The edit that must redden this criterion

fixture_matrix.description: For a criterion governing a COMPOUND predicate, the cross product of cells its fixtures must cover. A battery can only mutate the code its fixtures reach; every fixture sitting in one cell of a conjunction is how a veto-grade defect survives a green battery.

unmutable.description: Criteria with genuinely no available mutation, labelled ON PURPOSE with the reason. Labelling one weak beats giving it a mutation line that implies coverage it does not have. Beware the common false member: a criterion discharged by something being WRITTEN DOWN (an impl-report quote, a provenance trace, a file-shape reading) reports rather than tests, and usually has an assertion available.

discharged_by.description: What stands in for a mutation: a human read, a provenance record, a structural impossibility

expected_survivor.description: The documented survivor required by evidence.md rule 3b. Confirm the assertion can DISTINGUISH the case before recording one: a survivor that survives because nothing looked is an unfalsifiable clause wearing the label.
